eras.label: Bronze Age
eras.blurb: The first written myths. Sumer, Egypt and Ugarit put gods into clay and stone, and the earliest names we can still read appear.

eras.label: Iron Age & Classical
eras.blurb: Homer, the Vedas and the Hebrew Bible take shape. The Mediterranean and Iranian pantheons reach the form later ages inherit.

eras.label: Late Antiquity
eras.blurb: Conversion and compilation. Norse, Slavic and Celtic material is written down largely by the Christians replacing it.

eras.label: Medieval
eras.blurb: Bestiaries, sagas and the Shahnameh. Myth is copied, systematised and moralised across Eurasia.

eras.label: Early Modern
eras.blurb: Conquest, print and collection. European encounter records, and distorts, mythologies across the Americas, Africa and the Pacific.

eras.label: Modern
eras.blurb: Folklorists, nationalists and novelists. Myth is catalogued as heritage and simultaneously rewritten as entertainment.

eras.label: The Axial Age
eras.blurb: Within a few centuries and without contact, Greece, the Ganges plain, China and Persia each turned to asking how one ought to live. The single strangest coincidence in intellectual history.

eras.label: Hellenistic & Classical
eras.blurb: Schools become institutions. Stoics, Epicureans and Sceptics compete for the good life in the Mediterranean while Nyāya sharpens logic in India and Legalism hardens statecraft in Han China.

eras.label: Late Antiquity
eras.blurb: Philosophy meets revealed religion. Neoplatonism runs through Augustine into Christian thought; Nāgārjuna's emptiness reshapes Buddhism across Asia.

eras.label: Islamic Golden Age
eras.blurb: Baghdad, Bukhara and Córdoba inherit and extend the Greeks. Falsafa carries Aristotle forward while Śaṅkara systematises Advaita and Buddhism transforms in China.

eras.label: Scholastic & Medieval
eras.blurb: The university is invented. Aquinas, Ibn Rushd and Maimonides argue over the same inherited Aristotle in three languages, while Zhu Xi rebuilds Confucianism as metaphysics.

eras.label: Renaissance & Reformation
eras.blurb: Authority fractures. Humanists go back to the sources, printing spreads dissent faster than it can be suppressed, and the world turns out to be larger than the maps.

eras.label: Early Modern
eras.blurb: Descartes restarts philosophy from doubt. Rationalists and empiricists divide over where knowledge comes from, and the new physics forces everyone to answer to it.

eras.label: Enlightenment
eras.blurb: Kant tries to end the quarrel by mapping the limits of reason itself. Political philosophy stops being theory and starts becoming revolutions.

eras.label: The Nineteenth Century
eras.blurb: History, economics and suspicion enter philosophy. Marx, Mill, Kierkegaard and Nietzsche each attack a different pillar of the inherited picture.

eras.label: The Twentieth Century
eras.blurb: Analytic and continental traditions drift apart. Logic, language, phenomenology and existentialism split the discipline into conversations that stop hearing each other.

eras.label: Contemporary
eras.blurb: The map fills in outside Europe again. Ethics goes practical (minds, machines, climate, justice) and the old regional boundaries start to look accidental.
